ngs-DI3564.description: The NOAA CORS station nearest LC-39A that NGS publishes in both NAD83(2011) and ITRF: about 17 km south-south-east of the pad (NGS's radial search for CORS within 30 miles of N283630 W0803615: Cape Canaveral 1 to 6 at 10.8 to 10.9 miles, Titusville at 13.3). None is within a few kilometres. The datasheet gives NAD83(2011) only; the coordinate file gives both, the NAD83(2011) position transformed by NGS from ITRF2020 in April 2025. geodesy.noaa.gov/corsdata/ answered HTTP 410 (retired 2026-11-01), so the coordinate file is read from NGS's NOAA Open Data Dissemination bucket, the location NGS's data page gives. The two positions are not independent: NGS transformed the NAD83(2011) one from the ITRF2020 one, so a check between them tests PROJ's transformation against NGS's own computation (a published reference), not a measurement. The datasheet prints the ellipsoid height's adjustment date as "(04/??/25)": the "??" is NGS's own (no day), copied as printed.

lc-39a-pad.description: Where the robot arm's pad frame is defined (scenarios/arm.ts PAD): an input, not an expected value (ruling F6). AK1155 is a disk set in LC-39A's concrete pad, 24 feet south-south-west of the flame deflector's south-east corner (the datasheet's description). Its NAD83(1990) position is taken as NAD83(2011) at 2010.0 (an identity PROJ states at 0.1 m, ESRI:108355) and its ellipsoidal height is the datasheet's NAVD88 height plus its GEOID18 height. It is carried to 2026.0 by CCV6's NAD83(2011) velocity (borrowed from the station 17 km away; a passive mark has none of its own), then through PROJ's NAD83(2011) to ITRF2020 operation at 2026.0; arm.ts pins the result, which the data test holds to that path. NASA's fact sheet gives the Pad A hardstand as 48 feet above sea level, which agrees with the mark's 46.38 feet to within the step from the apron to the hardstand; it is cited as a cross-check, not used. The pad frame is a definition: the answer's ± is the arm's and the station's from this point, not a survey of LC-39A.

ifc43-map-conversion.definition: a scaling of the three axes (x,y,z), by the same IfcMapConversion.Scale, followed by an anti-clockwise rotation about the z-axis of θ, where θ = arctan(XAxisOrdinate / XAxisAbscissa), and then a translation in (x,y,z) of IfcMapConversion.Eastings, IfcMapConversion.Northings, IfcMapConversion.OrthogonalHeight
ifc43-map-conversion.xAxisAbscissa: Specifies the value along the easting axis of the end point of a vector indicating the position of the local x axis of the engineering coordinate reference system.
ifc43-map-conversion.xAxisOrdinate: Specifies the value along the northing axis of the end point of a vector indicating the position of the local x axis of the engineering coordinate reference system.
ifc43-map-conversion.scale: If omitted, the value of 1.0 is assumed.

cfr-33-167-off-san-francisco.description: The inbound lanes the ship's synthetic track follows (scenarios/vehicles.ts SHIP): an input, not an expected value (ruling F6). No AIS extract of one vessel small enough to pin (20 MB) was found: NOAA's daily AIS files are hundreds of megabytes, so the track is synthetic and labelled so.
cfr-33-167-off-san-francisco.track: The explorer's track: the northbound lane's centreline (122-39.80W) from 37-33.00N to 37-39.20N; across the precautionary area to the eastbound lane's start (37-45.85N 122-37.85W, midway between its two lines); along the lane's centreline through 37-46.893N 122-34.30W to 37-47.95N 122-30.90W; at 12 knots.

source.document: United States Coast Pilot 7, Pacific Coast — California, 2026 (58th) Edition
source.locator: Chapter 7 (San Francisco Bay), page 283, paragraph (195): "Alcatraz Light (37°49'34"N., 122°25'20"W.), 214 feet above the water" (a gray octagonal pyramidal tower on the island's southeast part); Chapter 1, paragraph (40), Heights: "in feet (meters) above the tidal datum used for that purpose on the charts, usually mean high water"

noaa-coast-pilot-7-alcatraz-light.description: The lighthouse the ship's mast looks for (scenarios/vehicles.ts LIGHTHOUSE): an input, not an expected value (ruling F6). The USCG Light List (Volume VI) is the primary source for a light's position and height, but navcen.uscg.gov answered HTTP 403 (and timed out) to the fetch, so the Coast Pilot's published entry is used; its chapter 1 is CPB7_C01_WEB.pdf (SHA-256 541a4003c12d684aa71e39a90b4d0befea9a036ffa50eb24d9635163518f4bec). The position is on NAD 83 to the nearest second (about ±15 m); the height is to the nearest foot, above mean high water. Not for navigation.

source.publisher: NOAA, Center for Operational Oceanographic Products and Services (CO-OPS), metadata API
source.locator: datums.json, units metric: epoch 1983-2001 (National Tidal Datum Epoch), accepted Apr 17 2003; MHW 3.416 m and NAVD88 1.804 m above the station datum (STND)

noaa-coops-9414290-datums.description: Carries the lighthouse's height from mean high water to NAVD88 (scenarios/vehicles.ts LIGHTHOUSE.mhwAboveNavd88: MHW − NAVD88 = 1.612 m): an input, not an expected value. NOAA states no accuracy for the offset; the example estimates ±0.05 m (Alcatraz is 4 km from the gauge, and mean high water drifts by centimetres across the central bay), labelled as an estimate.
